entities.name: WHO foodborne WGS guide: module 1 — introductory module
entities.description: Minimum epidemiological, laboratory and food-safety capacity needed before introducing whole-genome sequencing for foodborne disease surveillance and response.

entities.name: WHO foodborne WGS guide: module 2 — outbreak investigations
entities.description: How whole-genome sequencing can support investigations of foodborne disease outbreaks detected by existing surveillance systems, for countries beginning laboratory-based surveillance of selected foodborne pathogens.

entities.name: WHO foodborne WGS guide: module 3 — routine surveillance
entities.description: Using whole-genome sequencing for routine foodborne disease surveillance, outbreak detection, trend monitoring, and antimicrobial-resistance and virulence-factor monitoring.

entities.name: WHO global genomic surveillance strategy for pathogens with pandemic and epidemic potential, 2022–2032
entities.description: An end-to-end framework for strengthening pathogen genomic surveillance, including sample collection, diagnostics, data sharing and analysis across disease programmes and surveillance networks.

entities.name: WHO guide to developing a national genomic surveillance strategy or action plan
entities.description: Step-by-step considerations for national and subnational stakeholders developing a genomic surveillance strategy or action plan for pathogens with pandemic and epidemic potential.

entities.name: WHO guiding principles for pathogen genome data sharing
entities.description: Principles for sharing pathogen genome data to support detection, response, endemic-disease monitoring and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance.

entities.name: WHO guide to implementing SARS-CoV-2 genomic sequencing for public health
entities.description: Laboratory guidance on implementing SARS-CoV-2 genome sequencing for public-health impact, with relevance to emerging pathogens.
